name: TCL Google TV (G10/55C655) OTA Update Installation Without Removable Media — Reverse-Engineering Study
description: Reproducible reverse-engineering study showing that a vendor-signed OTA package cannot be installed on a TCL Google TV (Realtek RTD platform, Android TV 12) without a USB block medium, the vendor OTA server, or the vendor signing key. Documents the /cache bottleneck for non-A/B packages, the A/B payload path, signature enforcement, and the negative result of an exhaustive file-writer search across shipped apps. All device identifiers redacted (GDPR).

about.name: TCL Google TV firmware update mechanism (Realtek RTD platform)
A/B OTA payload handling and the /cache recovery bottleneck

findings: A vendor-signed OTA cannot be installed without one of: USB block medium, vendor OTA server, or vendor signing key.
/cache (93 MB) is the bottleneck for non-A/B packages (~1974 MB); A/B packages bypass it via uncrypt block maps.
RecoverySystem.verifyPackage() enforces a whole-file signature; not bypassable without the vendor key.
No external file writer to system install locations exists in the shipped applications (exhaustive search).
CVE-2025-55971 (blind SSRF in UPnP AVTransport) is real but not usable for update manipulation.
